ogTitle: Where to Eat in Khao Yai — Farm Steaks, Vineyard Dining, Cafes & Milk Treats
ogDesc: Restaurants that are actually open in Khao Yai and Pak Chong, with neighborhoods and ballpark prices — from farm steakhouses and wineries to fresh-milk souvenirs.
intro: Khao Yai and Pak Chong are about more than mountains and cool air — the food scene here is unusually varied. You've got steakhouses that raise their own cattle, restaurants sitting right in the vineyards where you sip wine with a view, mountain-view cafes you can linger in all day, and fresh-milk souvenirs people stop for on every trip. Here's what's on offer, which area it's in, and roughly what it costs.

blocks.html: Khao Yai's food roughly splits into four groups: steaks and grills from local cattle farms, vineyard restaurants that come with a view and their own wine, mountain-view cafes built around atmosphere, and the fresh-milk and yogurt souvenirs that Pak Chong has been known for for years. We've picked spots that are genuinely still open and steadily busy, with the area and price range so you can plan before you set off.

blocks.text: Farm steaks — beef from cattle raised right here

blocks.html: What sets Khao Yai steaks apart is that many places sit near or inside their own cattle farms, so the beef is fresh and quality is managed from the source. Prices run wide, from mains in the low hundreds of baht up to premium cuts in the thousands, so you can pick by budget and occasion.

items.name: Chokchai Steakhouse — inside Farm Chokchai
items.blurb: Pak Chong's legendary steakhouse, set inside Farm Chokchai, with beef from the farm's own cattle and house-reduced sauces. It's the kind of place families stop at every time they pass through. Weekend lunches get packed, so leave room for a wait.
items.meta: Farm Chokchai area, Mittraphap Rd km 159–160

items.name: Studer Restaurant — Josper Grill
items.blurb: One of the first Khao Yai steakhouses to use a Josper charcoal oven, so the beef carries a real smoky char. The room feels considered and works well for a special meal — book ahead on long weekends.
items.meta: Khao Yai area, near Thanarat Rd

items.name: Steak in Khao Yai
items.blurb: A steak-meets-Isan restaurant that's been part of Khao Yai for over a decade. Easy on the wallet and good for eating in a group without making a big deal of it.
items.meta: Thanarat Rd, on the way up to Khao Yai

blocks.title: Before you head to a famous steakhouse
blocks.html: Spots inside Farm Chokchai and other well-known places fill up at Saturday–Sunday lunch and on long weekends. If you're going then, call to book or arrive early, and be ready to wait in line.

blocks.text: Vineyard restaurants — eat with the rows of vines in view

blocks.html: Khao Yai is a wine-growing area with vineyards open to visitors and real restaurants on site. The draw is eating among the vines with the mountains around you, and many places pour their own wine to pair with the food. Good for a relaxed meal anytime from morning to evening.

items.name: GranMonte Vineyard & Winery — VinCotto restaurant
items.blurb: A vineyard of over 90 rai in the Asoke Valley, with the VinCotto restaurant serving homemade-style French food alongside the estate's own wine. You eat looking out over the rows of vines and the surrounding hills, it's open from breakfast through evening, and there are wine-tasting tours too.

items.name: PB Valley Khao Yai Winery
items.blurb: A large estate of more than 2,000 rai, with the vineyard open for tours and cycling. There's a restaurant with vineyard views where you can settle in for a long meal — a popular stop for wine lovers.
items.tag: Thanarat Rd · separate vineyard tour fee

blocks.title: On wine and driving
blocks.html: If you plan to taste wine at a vineyard, have a non-drinking driver or use a shuttle service. The roads into the vineyards and up to Khao Yai are winding in places, and driving impaired is a serious risk.

blocks.text: Mountain-view cafes — sit back in the cool air

blocks.html: Khao Yai has dozens of cafes scattered along Thanarat Rd and the surrounding zones. The selling point is the view of the hills and grassland, plus air that's cooler than Bangkok. Some go for a European-castle look, others are farms with animals for kids to meet — pick whatever style you like.

items.name: Midwinter Khaoyai
items.blurb: A cafe designed like a European castle, photogenic from every angle, with both a coffee zone and a food zone. It stays open into the evening, so it works for a daytime or sunset stop.

items.name: Toscana Valley cafe zone
items.blurb: An Italian-style zone with several cafes and restaurants in one area. You can wander and shoot photos with the hills behind you — a good mid-morning stop.

items.name: Sheep & alpaca farm cafe (Sheep Land / farm zone)
items.blurb: A farm cafe with sheep and alpacas you can feed — kids love it. There's a separate entry fee for the farm zone on top of your drinks. Good for families.

blocks.html: When people talk Khao Yai souvenirs, milk comes to mind first, because Pak Chong is a major dairy-farming area. Fresh milk, yogurt, ice cream, and milk tablets are the usual stops — easy on the wallet and simple to haul home.

items: Umm!..Milk (Farm Chokchai) — Farm Chokchai's own milk shop, with pasteurized fresh milk, yogurt, fresh-milk ice cream, and the popular milk tablets souvenir. Open roughly 9:00–17:00.
Dairy Home — Khao Yai's organic milk brand, with both a sit-down shop and souvenirs. Known for fresh milk, yogurt, and ice cream; it gets packed on weekends.
Pak Chong souvenir shops — along Mittraphap Rd you'll find souvenir shops carrying milk toffee, milk tablets, and milk-based sweets, so you can pick from several vendors in one spot.

blocks.title: Taking fresh milk home
blocks.html: Pasteurized fresh milk needs to stay chilled and has a short shelf life, so if you're driving far, buy it near the end of the trip and bring a cooler bag. Milk tablets and milk toffee keep longer and are better if you're buying a lot to give away.

blocks.text: How to plan a day of eating in Khao Yai

blocks.html: If you've got one day to eat and explore, try arranging it like this so you're not doubling back and you dodge the traffic crunch.

blocks.label: A day of eating in Khao Yai
blocks.title: Morning to evening

items.activity: Start at GranMonte or PB Valley vineyard
items.note: It's still cool — walk the vineyard and have a breakfast or brunch at the on-site restaurant before the sun gets harsh.
Arrive a little before noon to beat the line, especially on weekends.
Pick by style — a castle for photos, or a farm with animals if you've got kids along.

items.activity: Grab milk souvenirs before heading home
items.note: Buy fresh milk and milk tablets last, and bring a cooler bag if you're driving far.

blocks.title: Take care driving in the national park
blocks.html: If you're heading into Khao Yai National Park, the roads inside are winding and wildlife crosses often — elephants and deer especially. Drive slowly and don't honk to shoo animals away. There's an entry fee for people and vehicles at the posted rates, and after rain the trails to the waterfalls get slippery, so watch your footing.

faq.q: What food in Khao Yai should I try?
faq.a: The first things people think of are farm steaks like Chokchai Steakhouse, vineyard restaurants like GranMonte and PB Valley, mountain-view cafes, and fresh-milk and milk-tablet souvenirs from Umm!..Milk and Dairy Home.

faq.q: Which Khao Yai vineyard restaurant is best?
faq.a: GranMonte in the Asoke Valley has the VinCotto restaurant serving French food with the estate's own wine, while PB Valley is a large estate with a vineyard-view restaurant and vineyard tours. At both you eat looking out over the rows of vines and the hills.

faq.q: Where do I buy Khao Yai milk souvenirs, and roughly how much?
faq.a: Umm!..Milk inside Farm Chokchai and Dairy Home are the two main names, with fresh milk, yogurt, ice cream, and milk tablets. Prices are easy — milk tablets come in small packs from the tens up to a few hundred baht and make good gifts.

faq.q: What should I watch out for on a Khao Yai food trip?
faq.a: On long weekends the popular places get busy and accommodation fills up fast, so book ahead. The roads up the mountain and inside the park are winding with wildlife crossing, so drive slowly — and if you're tasting wine at a vineyard, have a non-drinking driver.

faq.q: Can I take Khao Yai fresh milk home?
faq.a: Yes, but pasteurized fresh milk needs to stay chilled and has a short shelf life, so buy it near the end of the trip and bring a cooler bag. Milk tablets and milk toffee keep longer and are better if you're buying a lot.
